purpose: Track GHAMOD (SOUTHMOD Ghana, EUROMOD engine) oracle-side behaviours that affect household-level Axiom comparisons for rulespec-gh. These are observations of the model's outputs, not statutory encoding gaps: in each the encoded RuleSpec follows current Ghana law and GHAMOD is the simplified oracle. The SOUTHMOD bundle is licensed and non-redistributable; entries describe observed behaviour and reference variable names and GHAMOD-produced values only, never model content.

entries.summary: GHAMOD's simulated labour income tax tin_s applies only five marginal-rate bands and taxes chargeable income above 238,760 GHS at a flat 30%, never applying the 35% top marginal rate that the Income Tax (Amendment) (No. 2) Act 2023 (Act 1111) introduced on income exceeding 605,000 GHS (labelled 600,000 in the First Schedule). Observed live: at chargeable income 700,000 GHS GHAMOD returns tin_s = 193,244 while the encoded Act 1111 schedule returns 197,994; the 4,750 difference is exactly 5% of the 95,000 above 605,000 that GHAMOD taxes at 30% rather than 35%. The two engines agree to the cedi for all chargeable income at or below 605,000. The encoded rulespec-gh schedule is statutorily correct; GHAMOD is the simplified oracle.

GHAMOD does not model the Act 896 Fifth Schedule paragraph 1(f) professional/technical/vocational training relief: its tinta04 relief is inactive and no tinta04_s output column is produced (a missing column, not a zero), so there is no GHAMOD value to compare against. The encoded rulespec-gh training_personal_relief pays min(cost, 2,000 GHS) per Act 896 as amended by Act 1007 and is exercised by the module's companion tests. Because the missing column cannot form a clean per-case comparison, the gh-personal-reliefs suite carries no live training case; the concept stays mapped (unused) in concept_mappings.yaml for the day a SOUTHMOD release models it.

GHAMOD splits the Act 896 Fifth Schedule paragraph 1(a) 'dependant spouse or at least two dependant children' relief into two limbs: a dependent-spouse relief tinta01 and a lone-parent relief tinta02. tinta01 fires correctly (1,200 GHS, observed) and is the parity case for the encoded dependant_spouse_or_children_personal_relief. tinta02 did not fire for any synthetic lone-parent household tested (a formal-sector earner with two dependent children under 19 linked by idmother or idfather, single or divorced marital status); those households instead received only the separate child-education relief tinta05. The encoded RuleSpec grants the 1,200 GHS relief for dependant_child_count >= 2 per Act 896 paragraph 1(a); the lone-parent limb is compared through the dependent-spouse limb, and the two-child limb is recorded here rather than asserted against a non-firing oracle output.

entries.observed: GHAMOD's tscee_gh/tscer_gh restrict SSNIT contributions to formal earners aged 15-45: a probed age-50 formal earner (lfo=1, positive yem) gets tscee_s = tscer_s = 0, while an otherwise identical age-35 earner gets exactly 5.5%/13% of yem. Population scale: 537 formal earners in gh_2017_a8 (weighted ~317k) fall outside the window.
entries.axiom_position: Act 766 s.3 imposes the worker and employer contributions on every worker's salary with no upper age limit; the encoded module (rulespec-gh gh/statutes/act-766/national-pensions-2008/section-3-contributions-to-the-scheme.yaml) follows the statute. The gh-ssnit-contributions suite therefore keeps its live cases inside the shared 15-45 window and records this entry for the out-of-window divergence.
entries.reported_upstream: Included in the SSNIT finding set drafted for UNU-WIDER (southmod@wider.unu.edu) alongside the tin_s top-band and relief findings.

entries.statute: Income Tax Act, 2015 (Act 896) First Schedule paragraph 8(1)(b); Act 907 s.1
entries.observed: GHAMOD's tinkt_gh withholds a flat 15% on investment income (tiniy_s = 0.15 x yiy, eligibility yiy > 50/yr; probed live: 1,000 of post-uprating yiy -> 150.00). No in-force paragraph 8(1)(b) rate supports 15% for investment income proper: dividends are 8% (row (i)); interest paid to an individual by a resident financial institution or on Government of Ghana bonds is exempt (Act 907 s.7(1)(p)/(q)) with a 1% residual row (ii); other interest is 8% (row (iii)). The 2015-2026 amendment chain is closed (all eleven Income Tax (Amendment) Acts read); none amended these rows. 15% exists only for non-residential rent and natural-resource/royalty rows.
entries.axiom_position: The encoded module (rulespec-gh gh/statutes/act-896/income-tax-2015/first-schedule-8-rates-of-withholding-tax.yaml) follows the statutory rows. The gh-capital-income suite compares rent (tinrt_s, 8%, exact) live and records this entry instead of running yiy cases, which would all diverge.
entries.reported_upstream: Queued for the UNU-WIDER finding set (southmod@wider.unu.edu) as finding #6 alongside the tin_s top-band, relief, and SSNIT age-cap findings.

entries.statute: Income Tax Act, 2015 (Act 896) Second Schedule paragraph 5, as substituted by Act 902 (2015) and Act 1071 (2021)
entries.observed: GHAMOD's ttn_gh restricts the presumptive turnover tax (3%) and the CHRL component (1%) to turnover between 10,000 and 120,000. Probed live: turnover 15,000 -> ttn01_s+ttn02_s = 450+150/yr although the statutory floor is 'more than twenty thousand' in every printed version; turnover 200,000 -> 0 although the in-force band (Act 1071, Dec 2021) runs to five hundred thousand Ghana Cedis (statute charges 6,000 + levy). The 120,000 ceiling matches only the original 2015 text, superseded within the same month by Act 902 (200,000); the 10,000 floor appears in no print. Inside the shared (20,000, 120,000] band the 3%/1% rates are exact (probed 30k/60k/120k -> 900/1,800/3,600 + 300/600/1,200).
entries.axiom_position: The encoded modules (rulespec-gh act-1071 second-schedule-substitutions; act-1068 section-1-imposition-of-levy) follow the in-force texts. The gh-presumptive-turnover suite keeps live cases inside the shared band and records this entry for the band divergence.
entries.reported_upstream: Queued for the UNU-WIDER finding set (southmod@wider.unu.edu) as finding #7.

entries.statute: Value Added Tax Act, 2013 (Act 870) chain (2025 cascade: levies 6% + VAT 15% on the levy-inclusive value = 21.9% of the standard base)
entries.observed: On a single standard-rated COICOP item (x0111105) with matching xhh, monthly base 1,000 (GH_2025): tva01_s/tva02_s/tva03_s = 25/25/10 (2.5%/2.5%/1%, correct); the pre-sum VAT component of tva_s is 210 (runtime $VAT_rate = 0.21, an effective-cascade shortcut; the base parameter column shows 0.15); the final ArithOp re-adds the three levy components (tva_s = 270 = 27%); and the ils_taxco stats list (tva_s + tva01 + tva02 + tva03 + ils_excise) adds them a third time (330 = 33%). GH_2024 shows the same pattern (237.10 / 878 base). Statutory 2025 wedge: 21.9%. tva_tex_cbs_gh is sw=off and not involved.
entries.axiom_position: The encoded 2026 modules (Act 1151 VAT 15%; Act 1152 GETFund 2.5%; Act 1156 NHIL 2.5%) follow the reform texts; rates carry unchanged across the boundary, so the gh-vat-levies suite compares the two levies against tva01_s/tva02_s exactly and dispositions the VAT/total comparison under this entry — GHAMOD emits no pure-VAT output.
entries.reported_upstream: Queued for the UNU-WIDER finding set (southmod@wider.unu.edu) as finding #8 — the largest-magnitude finding so far (~5 to ~11 points of the standard basket on any tva_s/ils_taxco statistic).
